# Guided and escorted swims. Dave, 2026-08-06: "this is a global list of
# SWIMS — guided is a swim, SwimTrek, swim holidays, those are all swims."
# SwimTrek runs trips across Asia and would land as swim_routes rather than
# dated events, but probe it the same way: the question is still what it
# actually publishes.
GLOBAL
# Not one of these yields a dated event through the deterministic
# extractors. Detail:
#   Ahotu (all 12 country URLs)  HTTP 403 — blocks automated fetches.
#       This was the prize: a global aggregator with a clean per-country
#       URL pattern, the Asian equivalent of what active.com does
#       elsewhere. Not retried and not worked around — a 403 is an answer.
#       Worth ASKING them for access; they are a commercial calendar and
#       may have a feed.
#   Singapore Aquatics           Calendar is an external Excel file linked
#       from the page. Nothing to crawl.
#   WOWSA Japan, Swim Maldives, Open Water Swims India, Swimming
#   Federation of India         Reachable, no usable dates on the listing.
#   SwimTrek                     Dates are loaded by JavaScript — zero
#       date-like strings in the raw HTML. Would need the renderer, and
#       its trips are swim_routes rather than dated events anyway.
#   Events Horizons (HK)         The probe says "no dates". The probe is
#       WRONG here, and this is the finding worth carrying: the raw HTML
#       contains "24th MAY 2026", and parseFreeTextDate reads it
#       correctly. The date sits in a Squarespace div that no deterministic
#       selector reaches, and probe-sources.ts runs only the deterministic
#       extractors — never the AI fallback the real crawler has. So a
#       "no-dates" verdict means "not deterministically extractable", NOT
#       "this page has no dates". Already enabled as a source; 1 published.
